Welcome from the Principal
As Principal, I believe passionately in the importance of the individual.
Every child at Brighton College is valued for his or her own sake and encouraged to develop his or her talents to the full. If you were to ask current parents why they chose Brighton College for their child, they would tell you the pupils here are cheerful, balanced, at ease with themselves and each other – yet excited and enthused by the challenges before them. They might add that the College succeeds in combining academic excellence with a wealth of opportunities, all underpinned by a deep commitment to the individual needs and enthusiasms of each child.
We were thrilled to be named United Kingdom School of the Decade by The Sunday Times, who praised the culture of kindness that underpins everything we do here.
The best way to get to know us is to come and visit. There are Open Mornings held throughout the year, and the pupils of Brighton College who will be your guides on the day are the best proof of everything contained in these pages. I could ask for no better ambassadors.
Richard Cairns, MA (Oxon)Principal
RICHARD CAIRNS, the only head in the UK to win TATLER HEAD OF THE YEAR TWICE

A Perfect Planting Party
A Perfect Planting Party
What a fantastic afternoon we had as our Nursery families joined their Puffin for a special planting party. The party started with plant pot decorating. The next job was to fill the pot with soil and make the very important decision as to which bulb to plant. It was then time to water the bulbs and write our names on a marker before placing our pots in the planting trays, ready for the planting magic to begin. The children also predicted what their flowers might look like by drawing chalk flowers on the playground and reading about how plants grow.

The Performing Arts
The Performing Arts
Specialist teaching in dance, drama and music is given to all pupils from Nursery to Year 6, helping to awaken a passion for performing arts.
The school is renowned for the high quality of its musicals and concerts. Each child can participate in shows and concerts throughout the year, helping to build confidence through music, dance and drama.
Our Performing Arts
Dance
Dance lessons are available from Nursery. Pupils from all year groups take to the stage in the Dance School’s stunning annual show. We offer a wide range of lessons, including Classical Ballet, Modern Dance, Contemporary, Hip Hop, Musical Theatre, Tap and Jazz.
Drama
Opportunities for drama include a thriving LAMDA programme. The school has its own drama studio and state-of-the-art theatre at the College, providing pupils with many opportunities to showcase their talents. Our pupils enjoy an excellent record in securing scholarships in the performing arts.
Music
Music is at the heart of school life for our musicians, offering a range of musical opportunities for pupils to learn and perform. From learning the recorder and ukulele to participating in choirs, orchestras, and masterclasses with renowned musicians, they are encouraged to develop a love for music and performance in a supportive and creative atmosphere.
Our Performances
Our performing arts departments work closely together to deliver a production programme in the College's new theatre and the Prep and Pre-Prep studios, from ensemble pieces and instrumental and jazz concerts to drama recitals and Dance Shows. Our popular Family Concert showcases the talent of our pupils to their parents, grandparents and extended family.

Nursery
The Perfect Start
The Nursery at Brighton College is where your child starts their educational journey.
Our caring and inspiring teachers deliver a dynamic and engaging Early Years curriculum that captures a child’s imagination. Your child will embark on their own journey of discovery and adventure during their time with us.
The Nursery classroom is purpose-built, bright and spacious, with access to an eco-friendly outdoor learning area, providing a free-flow learning space for your child to explore and discover. An integral part of our Prep, our Nursery provides the perfect start before moving to one of our Reception classes.
Small Numbers, Big Ideas
Children in the Nursery are introduced to an inspiring, creative and fun curriculum, enhanced by a wide variety of exciting learning opportunities. Small groups allow us to really get to know your child, ensuring they receive the highest level of individual attention to encourage their learning and growth.
Our Teachers
Our Early Years team consists of dedicated and experienced teachers who are passionate about nurturing young minds. Focusing on personalised care and attention, our highly qualified educators work closely with parents to ensure each child receives a unique and memorable learning experience.
Our School Day
Our Nursery pupils can be dropped off at school from 7:50am. A morning filled with learning through play awaits, and it includes the perfect mix of activities, including phonics, fine motor control, numeracy, art, cooking and music.
Our extensive outdoor learning environment provides plenty of outdoor play with ride-on toys, climbing equipment, sandpits, a mud kitchen and water play. Delicious and nutritious hot lunches are served every day.
Exciting Afternoons
Many children in our Nursery are ready to spend more than just a morning with us. We offer a range of optional themed afternoon activities that are perfect for little ones who are eager to continue exploring and learning.
Our themed afternoons provide engaging, hands-on opportunities that further enrich learning. From healthy food and cooking in Mini Chefs, a wellbeing focus in Harmony Heroes, to exploring beach school and nature in Waves and Wonder, staying active and developing early sports skills in Sporty Tots and developing coordination through Scoot, Cycle and Roll. Each experience nurtures children’s confidence, skills and curiosity while also fostering a strong sense of community through shared activities and collaboration.

Current Vacancies
To view and apply for current vacancies, please access our Careers Portal. Please direct any questions to recruitment@brightoncollege.net.
Work with Us
Career Opportunities
As The Sunday Times' Independent School of the Decade, The Sunday Times' Independent School of the Year and Britain's Most Forward-Thinking School (The Week), Brighton College is a leading school in England.
We take pride in employing passionate and talented individuals who wish to become part of our progressive community, offering professional development in a stimulating environment.
Why Work at Brighton College
Brighton College is renowned for its inspirational teaching and innovative education, whilst placing kindness and community at the heart of our approach to education.
Whether you're at the start of your career or an expert in your field, our reputation attracts incredible talent. We are proud of our staff and the contribution they make to the life of the school.
Life is Better by the Sea
Located in the vibrant city of Brighton, the College is a stone's throw from the sea and is close to the South Downs countryside, within easy travelling distance of London (about an hour by train), and about 30 minutes from Gatwick Airport. Portsmouth, Newhaven and the Channel Tunnel provide accessible links with the continent. Brighton is also a university city, and the College has good links with both the University of Sussex and Brighton University.
World-Class Facilities
At Brighton College, you will be working in a beautiful environment with world-class facilities. Whether it is teaching in one of our 18 university-standard science laboratories, taking your class to our on-site cinema or staging a performance in our incredible theatre, you'll have state-of-the-art facilities to inspire you and the pupils you teach. Our amazing body of support staff, without whom the College simply would not run, cover a wide range of roles across many departments.
Prioritising your Health and Happiness
We work closely with our staff to create a workplace that is well-balanced, fulfilling and joyful. Our wellbeing programme is open to all, offering activities such as yoga, Pilates and mindfulness. Further staff benefits include health assessments, a cycle-to-work scheme and a range of discount vouchers.
Staff Development
We have a rich programme of development and training opportunities throughout the year, relevant to your work and the College's needs. We encourage you to get involved and help you develop your career with us.
Equal Opportunities
We are proud to be an exceptionally forward-thinking and inclusive school, and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.
If you have passion and expertise in your chosen field, we want to hear from you.
Safeguarding
Brighton College is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.
Any offer of employment will be subject to an enhanced DBS disclosure, relevant original ID documentation and examination certificates. The College understands that a robust, fair and transparent recruitment and selection policy plays a central role in achieving this aim.
The College is committed to ensuring that the recruitment and selection of staff is conducted in a manner that is systematic, efficient and effective and promotes equality of opportunity.
Staff News
Our Staff
Current Vacancies
To view and apply for current vacancies, please access our Careers Portal. Please direct any questions to recruitment@brightoncollege.net.

The Creative Arts
The Creative Arts
Developing Creativity
At Brighton College, the creative arts give pupils the opportunity to think independently, explore ideas and develop their own visual voice in a purposeful and engaging environment. Through a broad and engaging curriculum, pupils are encouraged to experiment with materials and technologies, refine their techniques and approach their work with curiosity and imagination.
Working across a range of disciplines, pupils learn to observe closely, question creatively and take pride in the process of making. From initial sketches to finished pieces, the emphasis is on exploration, craftsmanship and the development of individual style, encouraging and supporting a range of artistic ambitions.
Our Creative Arts
Art
The art department encourages pupils to engage thoughtfully with the world around them, translating ideas into visual form through a wide range of media, including drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture and mixed media, developing both technical control and creative confidence.
We put emphasis on contemporary practice and theories that inform art, as well as practical skills. Lessons focus on experimentation and refinement, allowing pupils to explore different approaches while building a strong foundation in artistic practice. As they progress, pupils are encouraged to take increasing ownership of their work, producing outcomes that reflect their own interests and ideas.
Design and Technology
Design and Technology encourages pupils to think creatively and solve problems through making, with a focus on the quality and originality of ideas. Pupils consider functionality, aesthetics, user needs and sustainability as they develop thoughtful and well-crafted outcomes.
Working in a well-equipped workshop, pupils use both traditional tools and modern equipment to bring their ideas to life, often producing highly developed and, in many cases, award-winning work.
Projects guide pupils from initial concept through to final product, developing skills in design thinking, construction and evaluation. The emphasis is on precision, innovation and understanding how ideas can be realised in a practical and purposeful way.
Photography
Photography enables pupils to explore image-making as both a technical and creative discipline. Working in dedicated studio and darkroom spaces, pupils investigate all aspects of capturing an image, from experiencing traditional analogue processes alongside digital photography, editing and film.
Through a combination of practical work and creative projects, pupils learn how to compose, capture and manipulate images to communicate meaning, encouraging careful observation, attention to detail and a thoughtful approach to visual storytelling.
Our Artwork
Create in Outstanding Spaces
Pupils benefit from exceptional facilities that support creativity across a wide range of disciplines. Dedicated spaces for art, photography and design and technology provide an inspiring environment in which pupils can explore ideas, experiment with materials and refine their work.
Equipped with both traditional tools and modern technology, these spaces allow pupils to develop their skills with confidence and work in ways that reflect professional creative practice.
Opened in 2008, the Alexander Arts Centre is a large, loft-style studio and photography atelier. With an abundance of natural light within the space, pupils are able to explore their creativity in a variety of mediums. This includes access to a silkscreen printing room.
The RIBA award-winning Skidelsky Building houses our Design and Technology department. This is based in a multi-purpose workshop and design studio that incorporates the latest manufacturing machinery and equipment, as well as traditional tools and resources.
Located in the Alexander Arts Centre, our photography department caters for all mediums of image making. Pupils can engage with analogue, darkroom photography through to digital photoshop and film-making, alongside the more practical montage manipulation.
Exhibitions and Opportunities
Pupils regularly present their work in exhibitions and competitions, providing opportunities to reflect on their progress and share their ideas with others.
Events such as the Leonardo Creativity Competition encourage pupils to think ambitiously and explore new directions in their work. These experiences help to develop independence, critical thinking and a sense of pride in the creative process.

Creative arts at Brighton College are about more than producing finished work – they are about developing curiosity, independence and the confidence to think differently.
Through a wide range of opportunities at Brighton College, pupils are encouraged to explore their interests, experiment with new ideas and discover their own creative strengths.

The Performing Arts
Music, Drama and Dance
A Culture of Creativity and Confidence
At Brighton College, we believe that participation in the performing arts plays an important role in a pupil’s development. Through drama, music and dance, pupils are encouraged to build confidence, develop creativity and express themselves in a supportive and nurturing environment.
Whether taking weekly dance lessons, performing with our award-winning Chamber Choir, playing in a rock band in the House Music competition or taking centre stage in one of our many productions, pupils benefit from regular opportunities to perform. These experiences help to develop communication skills, build confidence and encourage thoughtful, creative self-expression.
Each year, we stage a wide range of musical, dramatic and dance performances, from informal concerts to large-scale productions. Pupils collaborate across year groups to create performances that celebrate imagination, teamwork and individuality. For many, these shared experiences become some of the most memorable and rewarding moments of their time at school.
Our Performing Arts
Music
Music is an important and vibrant part of school life, with opportunities for all pupils to get involved, regardless of experience. From percussion groups and swing bands, to the award-winning chamber choir and symphony orchestra, we offer musical opportunities for everyone on all orchestral instruments, voice, classical and electric guitar, harp, piano and organ.
Regular concerts, competitions, events and informal performances allow pupils to build confidence and enjoy sharing their progress with others, while fostering a lifelong appreciation of music. Our pupils go on to study music at the Royal Academy of Music, Oxbridge and Trinity College, London, among others.
Drama
Drama provides a safe and imaginative space in which pupils can explore ideas, build confidence and develop strong communication skills. Through a range of productions and class-based activities, pupils are encouraged to take part, whether performing on stage or contributing behind the scenes.
Pupils develop key skills such as teamwork, public speaking and creative thinking within a supportive environment that values participation as much as performance. We also offer LAMDA (London Academy of Music and Dramatic Arts) lessons, enabling all pupils to take part in drama, regardless of whether they pursue it as an academic subject.
Many pupils continue their interest in drama beyond school, with recent leavers going on to study at leading institutions including RADA, Mountview Academy of Theatre Arts, the Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts and Bristol Old Vic Theatre School.
Dance
Dance at Brighton College is energetic, inclusive and attracts pupils of all abilities, from complete beginners to experienced performers. With classes in hip hop, jazz, ballet, tap, modern and contemporary, there is something for everyone.
From learning basic steps to performing at festivals and international competitions, pupils are supported by a passionate and professional team who encourage both technical development and creative expression. Regular opportunities to perform, including in our highly popular annual Dance Show, allow pupils to build confidence and enjoy being part of a vibrant and collaborative community.
Performance Opportunities
Throughout the year, pupils take part in a wide range of performances, from plays and concerts to whole-school events that bring the community together. These occasions provide valuable opportunities for pupils to build confidence, work collaboratively and experience the enjoyment of performing in front of an audience. They also allow parents to share in and celebrate their children’s achievements.
Perform in Outstanding Facilities
Pupils benefit from excellent facilities that support creativity and performance, including dedicated spaces for drama, music and dance. These environments are designed to encourage participation, allowing pupils to rehearse, perform and develop their skills with confidence.
Our stunning 400-seat theatre is truly breathtaking, providing pupils with the opportunity to not only perform on a professional stage, but also gain theatre management experience.
With its professional sprung floor, floor-to-ceiling mirrors and ballet barres, our new and purpose-built Dance Studio is the perfect space for our budding dancers.
Our state-of-the-art Drama Studio provides the College with its own adaptable black box theatre. It provides an excellent teaching space, as well as being extremely adaptable for GCSE and A-level productions and smaller-scale plays and events.
In our RIBA award-winning Music School, our pupils enjoy professional rehearsal, recording and performance spaces.

More Than Performance
Performing arts at Brighton College are about far more than performance – they are about confidence, creativity and developing a love of learning. With a wide range of opportunities available at Brighton College, pupils are encouraged to explore their interests, try new activities and discover where their talents lie.
Book a visit or speak to our admissions team to see how you can become part of Brighton College. For pupils with particular talent in drama, music or dance, scholarships are available – find out more via the link below.

Brighton College Prep School Crowned 'Best Early Years in Britain'
Brighton College Prep School Crowned 'Best Early Years in Britain'
We are thrilled to announce that our Prep School has been awarded 'Best Early Years in Britain' at The Week Education Awards 2026.
These highly acclaimed awards look at the UK’s leading independent schools to find the ‘best of the best’ prep schools in the country.
Our Early Years has been commended for its specialist teaching in the arts, languages and sport, as well as our brilliant Beach School curriculum, where learning truly comes to life!
Our Headmaster of the Prep School, Mr Falkus, said: "This is a wonderful accolade for the Prep School, and I am incredibly proud of our teachers and wonderful pupils, whose enthusiasm makes our school such a special place to be".

Dancers Sparkle in Annual Showcase
Dancers Sparkle in Annual Showcase
We were delighted to welcome so many of you to Brighton Dome this Tuesday for our annual Dance Show! The Dance School celebrated a vibrant year of dance with pupils from the Pre-Prep, Prep, Lower and Senior Schools performing ballet, modern, contemporary, tap and jazz pieces.
In act one, the Senior Show Team started the show with Rhythm Nation, and The River to the Blue Sea Flows was performed by Senior Ballet Pupils and the Junior Show Team. This was followed by Game X and Rain on Me, with pupils performing high-energy commercial pieces. The act finished with the Senior Boys’ Squad performance of Footloose; it was great to see so many boys involved in the Dance Show!
Act two opened with tap pupils giving a spectacular performance of Hairspray, which was an exciting taste of the dances to come. This was followed by Stay, a duet from our two leaving ballet pupils, and another beautiful performance from our Senior Show Team of California Dreaming, and the contemporary pupils performing Heaven.
The show shifted atmosphere into cutting and electrifying performances from our leavers, the Senior and Advanced Commercial Jazz and Senior Hip Hop groups. Closing the show was our Senior Show Team and Modern pupils in an upbeat and fun Jazz Café, which ended with every modern dance pupil on stage for one final, proud jazz hands!
Congratulations to each and every one of the pupils involved in the production. The sense of enjoyment on stage was effervescent, and a huge thank you to Ms Linkenbagh and her dance team for their hard work in pulling together a truly magical show!

Nursery to Oxbridge
Nursery to Oxbridge
Building on the wonderful news of our Oxford offers, we are delighted to celebrate another outstanding achievement this week - 22 Sixth Form pupils have secured offers from the University of Cambridge.
Four of these pupils who received Oxbridge offers began their journey at our Prep School, including two who started in Nursery. Huge congratulations to Aster, who joined us in Nursery and has secured an offer to read Classics at Oxford; Jack, who arrived in Year 5 and will be studying Computer Science at Cambridge; Rafi, another pupil who started in Nursery and has been offered a place to read Classics at Cambridge; and Stan, who joined in Year 5 and has received an offer to study Geography at Cambridge.

Teddy Bears Picnic
Teddy Bears Picnic
Our Nursery pupils have been very busy preparing invitations for their Teddy Bears Picnic, popping them in envelopes and sticking them on stamps to send to their favourite bears so they can join in the picnic fun. Once the invites were written and safely in envelopes, the children, accompanied by their teachers, embarked upon a mini adventure to post them. They walked safely and sensibly to the nearest shiny red post box, where each eager little Puffin carefully posted their bear’s invitation.
When the picnic day arrived, the teddies and children thoroughly enjoyed teddy bear races, bubble-blowing, and some teddy bear chasing games. All the picnic goers were ready for a little mid-morning sustenance and tucked into their yummy homemade sandwiches with glee while listening to our favourite bear story; We’re Going on a Bear Hunt. With full tummies and tired teddies, we returned to school just in time for lunch. What a fun and fabulous morning.

The Peter Bellenger Memorial Challenge
The Peter Bellenger Memorial Challenge
It is a face that we shall always remember. The humour and the humility, the generosity and the modesty; Pete Bellenger was a man much adored at the College, but a life cut short by motor neurone disease. And almost a year on from his passing, we celebrated the beautiful life of our friend and former chemistry teacher with a memorial row: 100km along the Thames with Oxford the final port of call.
Setting off from Leander Club in Henley, the crew rowed the distance over two days, finishing at the New College, Oxford boathouse, where Pete had spent much of his timeas an undergraduate student.
The event hoped to honour Pete’s memory, particularly as the first-year anniversary of his death comes around, and to raise funds for the Motor Neurone Disease Association (MNDA) which gave Pete, his family and his friends so much support during his seven-year battle with Motor Neurone Disease.
Commencing last Friday morning in the charming town of Henley-on-Thames – scene of where Pete won the Lightweights Boat Race for Oxford – a collection of his closest friends, including our own Head of Senior School, Mr Marshall-Taylor, rowed the distance to Oxford, where Pete’s sister and parents were waiting to greet them.
Following the row, Mr Marshall Taylor added, "just as Pete would have wanted, it was full of laughter, new friendships and a sense of hope – hope that, when we all contribute our little bit and come together to do what we can, something significant, something remarkable can happen.
As Pete’s mum commented at the end, Pete himself would have loved the challenge as a celebration of so many things and so many people that he loved", he continued.
It was a quite brilliant achievement from those that took part in this wonderful event for an even better cause. Our ongoing support for the MNDA at the College continues to grow ever onwards, with pupils Charlotte and Ed having organised their own set of pupil House fundraising events. Those rowing the 100km stretch never could have imagined the enormous generosity of support, both in person, along the banks of the Thames and in Oxford, and through the fundraising website. The current total raised is over £125,500, a truly remarkable amount!

Years 7 and 8 Dazzle in Chitty Chitty Bang Bang
Years 7 and 8 Dazzle in Chitty Chitty Bang Bang
Our talented Year 7 and 8 pupils took to the stage with energy and remarkable skill to perform their Chitty, Chitty, Bang Bang production.
The audience was treated to a rollercoaster of emotions as they laughed, cried, cheered, and applauded the cast’s stellar performance of this classic musical. The extraordinary talent on display was complemented by the grandeur of colourful costumes and a showstopping set crafted by Mr Bates.
The entire production was a triumph, and witnessing the joy on the faces of the cast was a true delight. This unforgettable show has left a lasting impact, creating joyful memories for the audience, pupils, and crew alike.

The Creative Arts
The Creative Arts
We believe that nurturing a child's creativity is essential to their education.
That's why we offer a broad range of art and design technology classes to all pupils from Nursery to Year 6. By encouraging our pupils to express themselves creatively, we help them build their problem-solving, critical thinking and visual literacy skills.
Whether children have an interest in painting, printmaking, sculpting, or working on graphic design and technology projects, we provide abundant opportunities for them to develop a lifelong appreciation for the creative arts.
Our Creative Arts
Art
Our art curriculum from Nursery to Year 6 fosters creativity and self-expression in our pupils. Through various mediums and techniques, pupils explore and develop their artistic skills, gaining a deeper appreciation for the world of art.
Design and Technology
Our design and technology curriculum from Year 4 encourages pupils to explore design and engineering principles. Through hands-on projects, they learn to problem-solve, innovate, and create using a wide range of materials and tools.

pageCache.text:

The Creative Arts
The Creative Arts
Developing Your Creative Voice
At Brighton College, creative arts in the Sixth Form are about developing your own ideas, refining your technique and producing work that reflects your individuality.
Whether working in art, photography or design, you are encouraged to experiment, take creative risks and build a portfolio that reflects your interests and ambitions. From initial concepts to resolved outcomes, the focus is on independence, originality and the confidence to pursue your own direction.
You will explore a wide range of media, colour, form and texture in imaginative and challenging ways, combining traditional techniques with digital processes. This approach enables you to develop your work with increasing sophistication, preparing you for further study beyond school and the creation of exciting, thought-provoking outcomes.
Our Creative Arts
Art
Art in the Sixth Form is both exploratory and highly individual. You will work across a range of media, including painting, printmaking, sculpture and mixed media, developing the technical skill and critical understanding needed to support your ideas.
As your work progresses, you will take ownership of your projects, producing outcomes that reflect your own interests, influences and creative direction. The emphasis is on experimentation, refinement and the development of a strong personal visual language.
Design and Technology
Design and Technology allows you to turn ideas into fully realised outcomes, combining creativity with practical problem-solving.
Working with a range of materials, tools and processes, you will develop projects from initial concept through to final product. The focus is on innovation, precision and producing work that is both functional and well-resolved, preparing you for further study in design, engineering or related fields.
Photography
Photography offers the opportunity to explore image-making in depth, from analogue darkroom processes to digital photography, editing and film.
You will learn to construct and manipulate images with intention, developing a strong understanding of composition, lighting and visual narrative. Through sustained projects, you will build a portfolio that demonstrates both technical ability and a clear creative voice.
Our Artwork
Create in Outstanding Spaces
You will work in dedicated creative spaces designed to support a wide range of disciplines, from studio-based art and photography to hands-on making and design.
With access to both traditional tools and modern technologies, these environments allow you to experiment, refine your work and develop your ideas with confidence and independence.
The Alexander Arts Centre is a large, loft-style studio. With an abundance of natural light in the space, pupils are able to explore their creativity in a variety of mediums. This includes access to a silkscreen printing room.
Our RIBA award-winning Skidelsky Building houses our Design and Technology department. This is based in a multi-purpose workshop and design studio that incorporates the latest manufacturing machinery and equipment, as well as traditional tools and resources.
Located in the Alexander Arts Centre, our photography studio caters for all mediums of image making. Pupils can engage with analogue darkroom photography through to digital photoshop and filmmaking, alongside the more practical montage manipulation.
Exhibitions and Opportunities
There are regular opportunities to exhibit your work, both within the College and beyond, allowing you to present your ideas in a professional context and see your work realised at scale.
A highlight of the creative calendar is the annual Leonardo Creativity Competition, inspired by the ingenuity and artistic vision of Leonardo da Vinci. Open to pupils across all year groups, it celebrates creativity, innovation and collaboration, encouraging you to push your ideas further and think in new ways.
From emerging artists to more experienced creators, pupils explore ambitious concepts and produce original work across a range of disciplines. Winners across several categories receive prizes, with selected work exhibited in a Brighton art gallery.
These opportunities play an important role in developing your confidence, refining your portfolio and preparing your work for the next stage.

Your Creative Direction
Creative arts in the Sixth Form are not just about developing skills – they are about defining your own direction as a creative thinker.
Whether you are preparing for art school, a creative degree or simply pursuing a passion, you will be supported to produce work that is ambitious, individual and entirely your own.
Book a visit or speak to our admissions team to find out more about life at Brighton College. For pupils with particular talent in the arts, scholarships are available – find out more via the link below.
